title: Aamir Khan and Farhan Akhtar Are Reuniting for a Partition-Era Cricket Biopic — and It's Basically the Real *Lagaan*
excerpt: Twenty-five years after Lagaan, Aamir Khan teams up with Ashutosh Gowariker and Rajkumar Hirani for the story of Lala Amarnath, India's first Test captain. Farhan Akhtar is in talks to co-star.
body:
Exactly 25 years after they assembled a ragtag team of villagers to beat the British at cricket in *Lagaan*, Aamir Khan and director Ashutosh Gowariker are reuniting — and this time, the cricket story is real.

The pair are developing a biopic of **Lala Amarnath**, India's first Test captain and the man who scored the country's first-ever Test century in 1933, when he was just 22 years old. And in a move that has Bollywood buzzing, **Farhan Akhtar** is in advanced talks to join the project in a pivotal role.

## A Friendship Across Partition

According to sources close to the production, the film isn't just a straight cricket biopic. At its heart, it's a **friendship story set against the backdrop of Partition**.

Aamir will play Lala Amarnath himself. Farhan is being considered for the role of Amarnath's closest friend — a character who lived in undivided India but moved to Pakistan after 1947. "The emotional dynamics between the two characters form the heart of the narrative," a source told Pinkvilla.

The story comes from **Rajkumar Hirani**, with creative inputs from Hirani and his longtime collaborator **Abhijat Joshi** on the screenplay. The film is being produced jointly by Aamir Khan Films, Excel Entertainment, and Rajkumar Hirani. Production is expected to begin around **October 2026** with a start-to-finish schedule.

## Why Lala Amarnath Matters

For NRIs who grew up hearing about Sachin's centuries and Dhoni's World Cup six, Lala Amarnath's story is the origin myth they probably never learned in detail.

Born in **Lahore in 1911** — in what is now Pakistan — Amarnath became India's first Test centurion when he struck 118 against England at Bombay Gymkhana in December 1933. He went on to captain independent India's first Test team in 1947-48 and led the side to its **first-ever Test series victory against Pakistan in 1952**.

His life spanned the most turbulent decades of Indian history: colonial rule, the freedom movement, Partition, and the birth of two new cricket-playing nations. He was awarded the **Padma Bhushan** in 1991 and passed away in 2000 at the age of 88. His sons, **Mohinder Amarnath** (hero of the 1983 World Cup) and Surinder Amarnath, both went on to play Test cricket for India.

## The *Lagaan* Parallel

The reunion of Aamir and Gowariker carries enormous symbolic weight. *Lagaan* (2001) wasn't just a cricket film — it was India's entry for the Academy Awards and became a cultural touchstone for the diaspora. It was the film NRI families watched together at community screenings in New Jersey and Houston and London. If *Lagaan* was a fable about cricket as resistance, the Lala Amarnath biopic promises to be the **real history** that fable was built on.

With Hirani's storytelling instincts and Aamir's track record of physically transforming for roles (remember the body he built for *Dangal*, or the age transitions in *Laal Singh Chaddha*), this is shaping up to be one of the most ambitious Bollywood productions of 2027.

## What's Next for Aamir

The Lala Amarnath film is part of an unusually packed slate for Aamir, who is known for taking years between projects. He's also attached to **4 Idiots** (the *3 Idiots* sequel with Rajkumar Hirani) and a start-up drama directed by Rahul Mody. If all three go as planned, 2027-28 could be the most productive stretch of Aamir Khan's career in over a decade.

For the diaspora, the Lala Amarnath biopic hits a particular nerve: it's a story about a man who played for a country before it was even a country, whose birthplace ended up in another country, and whose legacy transcended borders. In an era when NRIs are more connected to Indian cricket than ever — streaming IPL at 4 AM, flying back for World Cup finals — this is the origin story that's been waiting to be told.
